page: Amazon Web Services inf2.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.6 GHz, configured with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core, totaling 4 virtual CPUs. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is not included, and network connectivity is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the top 25% at 2965.49. However, multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 5927.07 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 3748.0, which falls into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with both small-block cached read bandwidth (283.31 GB/sec) and large-block uncached read bandwidth (38.44 GB/sec) ranking in the bottom 25%.

For specialized tasks, the server achieves average performance in single-threaded gzip compression (28.93 GB/sec) and text processing, but shows weak performance in database operations, static web serving (5.62 GB/sec), and software compilation. LLM inference benchmarks using a small 135M model yield 153.84 tokens/sec for text generation, but performance drops significantly to 6.57 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model. Given the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, this instance provides an entry-level general-purpose environment, though it is constrained by low network bandwidth and weak memory throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services inf2.xlarge is an x86_64 server utilizing the Nitro hypervisor and a dedicated AMD EPYC 7R13 processor. It features 4 vCPUs, 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, with no local storage. Performance benchmarks show strong single-core CPU capabilities, scoring 2965.49 in stress-ng, but multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are generally weak, falling into the bottom 25%. The instance delivers average text processing and single-threaded compression performance, but struggles with database operations, static web serving, and larger LLM inference tasks. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads, basic text processing, and lightweight single-threaded applications that do not require high memory bandwidth or local storage.
